audit_logging_requirements_summary: Key ask: enterprise-grade audit trail exported to their SIEM (Splunk primary; Datadog secondary). Must support TCP/TLS syslog, CEF and JSON L2 formats, and S3 archival (immutable, versioned bucket) for 3+ years with legal hold. Logs must tie back to KMS key IDs, show encryption context, and include admin action events (policy changes, model rollouts, key rotation). Prompt-content retention policy: default redact PII, option to store hashed input_id + output_id for repro + evaluation. Must support streaming forwarders and batch export.
siem_export_details: Preferred methods: 1) Syslog TCP/TLS (CEF or JSON) to their Splunk forwarder; 2) HTTPS webhook with mutual TLS to Datadog/other; 3) Periodic S3 bucket export (encrypted with customer KMS) for cold storage. All transports must support mutual TLS and token-based authentication. Needs cert rotation docs and forwarder troubleshooting runbook.
retention_and_legal_controls: Requested retention windows: 90 days (hot), 3 years (warm), 7 years (cold/legal hold) with ability to place legal hold on specific request IDs. Must support configurable retention per log class (admin events = 7y, user prompts = 90d unless explicitly retained) and on-demand export for e-discovery. SLA for export and search: 24h for hot logs, 72h for warm retrieval.
access_and_monitoring_requirements: Audit must record who accessed logs and which queries were run (meta-audit). Access logs for the log store (S3 access logs, object-level) must be exported to SIEM. Role-based access for viewing raw prompts; CSM and AE will need demo of RBAC + sample redaction flows.
kms_integration_requirements: Customer-managed KMS required. Redwood must log key usage events (Encrypt/Decrypt/GenerateDataKey) with key IDs and encryption context. Support cross-account IAM roles for KMS access and HSM-backed keys. Rotation schedule must be visible in logs; provide proof-of-use for any rotated key used to encrypt archived logs.
risk_notes_and_concerns: Infosec worry: potential prompt leakage through logs and debug traces. Legal wants clear redaction & proof of deleted data. Network team: require static IPs for forwarders and AWS peering worksheet. Operations: want deterministic schema, stable field names to feed downstream parsers. Concern about performance impact of synchronous logging on latency-sensitive chat flows.
